answer.worked:
Multiply the first equation by $12$ and the second by $2$.

$$\begin{align*}4x+3y&=12\\3x-2y&=8\end{align*}$$

Multiply these equations by $2$ and $3$, respectively, then add.

$$\begin{align*}8x+6y&=24\\9x-6y&=24\\17x&=48\\x&=\frac{48}{17}\end{align*}$$

Substitute into $3x-2y=8$.

$$\begin{align*}3\left(\frac{48}{17}\right)-2y&=8\\-2y&=-\frac{8}{17}\\y&=\frac{4}{17}\end{align*}$$

Check:

$$\begin{align*}\frac{48/17}{3}+\frac{4/17}{4}&=\frac{16}{17}+\frac{1}{17}=1\\\frac{3(48/17)}{2}-\frac{4}{17}&=\frac{72}{17}-\frac{4}{17}=4\end{align*}$$

Multiply the first equation by $56$ and the second by $12$.

$$\begin{align*}16x+7y&=0\\9x-4y&=0\end{align*}$$

Multiply these equations by $4$ and $7$, respectively, then add.

$$\begin{align*}64x+28y&=0\\63x-28y&=0\\127x&=0\\x&=0\end{align*}$$

Substitute into $9x-4y=0$.

$$\begin{align*}9(0)-4y&=0\\y&=0\end{align*}$$

Both original equations have left-hand side $0$ when $x=0$ and $y=0$, so both are satisfied.
